source_text:
Καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι ἡμῶν ἔγνωσαν διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅτι ἔρις ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ ὀνόματος τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς.
διὰ ταύτην οὖν τὴν αἰτίαν πρόγνωσιν εἰληφότες τελείαν κατέστησαν τοὺς προειρημένους, καὶ μπταξὺ ἐπινομὴν δεδωκασιν, ὅπως, ἐὰν κοιμηθῶσιν, διαδέξωνται ἕτεροι δεδοκιμασμὲνοι ἅνδρες τὴν λειτουργίαν αὐτῶν.
τοὺς οὖν κατασταθέντας ὑπ’ ἐκείνων ἢ μεταξὺ ὑφ̓ ἑτέρων ἐλλογίμων ἀνδρῶν συνενδοκησάσης τῆς ἐκκλησίας πάσης, καὶ λειτουργήσαντας ἀμέμπτως τῷ ποιμνίῳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ μετὰ ταπεινοφροσύνης, ἡσύχως καὶ ἀβαναύσως, μεμαρτυρημένους τε πολλοῖς χρόνοις ὑπὸ πάντων, τούτους οὐ δικαίως νομίζομεν ἀποβάλλεσθαι τῆς λειτουργίας.
ἁμαρτία γὰρ οὐ μικρὰ ἡμῖν ἔσται, ἐὰν τοὺς ἀμέμπτως καὶ ὁσίως προσενεγκόντας τὰ δῶρα τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς ἀποβάλωμεν.
μακάριοι οἱ προοδοιπορήσαντες πρεσβύτεροι, οἵτινες ἔγκαρπον καὶ τελείαν ἔσχον τὴν ἀνάλυσιν: οὐ γὰρ εὐλαβοῦνται μή τις αὐτοὺς μεταστήσῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἱδρυμένου αὐτοῖς τόπου.
ὁρῶμεν γάρ, ὅτι ἐνίους ὑμεῖς μετηγάγετε καλῶς πολιτευομένους ἐκ τῆς ἀμέμπτως αὐτοῖς τετιμημένης λειτουργίας.
thought_title: Do not cast out blameless leaders
orientation: The writer from Rome argues that the apostles foresaw disputes over office and provided for approved successors, so removing blameless leaders is unjust.
pass_a_gloss: And our apostles knew through our Lord Jesus Christ that strife will be over the name of the bishop's office. For this cause therefore, having received complete foreknowledge, they appointed the aforementioned men, and afterwards they gave an additional instruction, in order that, if they fall asleep, other approved men may succeed to their ministry. Those therefore appointed by them or afterwards by other reputable men, with the whole church consenting, and having ministered blamelessly to the flock of Christ with humility, quietly and without vulgarity, and having been witnessed to for many years by all, these we consider it not just to cast out from the ministry. For it will be no small sin for us, if we cast out those who blamelessly and holily offered the gifts of the bishop's office. Blessed are the elders who went on ahead, who had a fruitful and complete departure; for they do not fear lest anyone move them from the place established for them. For we see that you transferred some who conducted themselves well out of the ministry that had been honored blamelessly for them.

choices.english: over the name of the bishop's office
choices.why: literal for ἐπί + genitive and keeps brief term for bishops rather than abstract oversight
required by brief glossary for λειτουργία in ordered church service
required by brief glossary for ταπεινοφροσύνη

choices.term: ἐκ τῆς ἀμέμπτως αὐτοῖς τετιμημένης λειτουργίας
choices.english: out of the ministry that had been honored blamelessly for them
choices.why: participle τετιμημένης is passive perfect with dative αὐτοῖς of advantage, so the honor was given to them, not done by them
rejected: from the ministry they had honored blamelessly

pass_b_english: Our apostles knew through our Lord Jesus Christ that strife would arise over the name of the bishop's office. For that reason they acted with complete foreknowledge: they appointed the men already described, and then left further instruction that, if those men fell asleep, other tested men should succeed to their ministry.

Those men were appointed either by the apostles or afterward by other reputable men, with the whole church consenting. They have served Christ's flock blamelessly, with humility, quietly and without baseness, and all have spoken well of them for many years. We do not consider it right to cast such men out from the ministry. For it will be no small sin for us if we cast out those who have offered the gifts of the bishop's office blamelessly and holily.

Blessed are the elders who have gone on ahead, whose departure was fruitful and complete. They do not fear that anyone will move them from the place secured for them. But we see that you have moved some who lived honorably from the ministry that had been blamelessly honored for them.
notes: Source reads μπταξὺ for expected μεταξὺ and ἐπινομὴν; glossed as afterwards and additional instruction; taken as transmission misprint, not invented text.
